text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: GPU queue growth > 3k across us-west-2 pools, autoscaler at hard limit. Paging on-call (pamela). :rotating_light:

pamela: I'm on it. seeing spike in request_queue_size -> 4240, avg_wait=48s, p95_wait=102s. Which pools are hit?

sanjay: west-gpu-pool-a and west-gpu-mig-slice-1. Autoscaler reports node_count=120 (max), can't scale.

ana: (ana) adding logs: scheduler shows many small jobs pinned to large MIG slices, binpacking inefficient. lots of free GPU lanes but not usable due to MIG sizing mismatch.

pamela: so we have stranded capacity, not shortage of raw GPUs. what's the stranded count?

kevin: quick metric: ~24 full GPUs equivalent stranded across pools due to incompatible MIG templates and small-job fragmentation. utilization on affected nodes ~22%.

tier2-ops-bot: Alert: queue_growth_rate > 2000/min in last 5m. Throttling kicked in for lower tier customers.

maria: Customer-impact: several enterprise routes returning 503s & timeouts. CS notified top 3 customers, they're seeing request failures and high latency.

customer-success: Confirmed. Two customers on Dedicated reported failures; ticket opened. They're asking for ETA.

pamela: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) enable burstpool on affected pools, 2) evict/shift low-priority batch jobs, 3) temporarily raise autoscaler max (requires approval), 4) trigger manual repack/rebalance to merge fragmented capacity. Thoughts?

sanjay: Repacking helps but takes time and causes evictions. Eviction ramp will momentarily increase queue. Burstpool for short-term is lowest-risk.

ana: We can also fall back some traffic to smaller model-quantized variants to reduce GPU needs. However that requires routing changes in control plane (can be fast for hosted).

kevin: Manual MIG resize (change slice templates to smaller slices) would free small-job placement but it's risky mid-incident; needs coord with infra and may require node reboots.

pamela: OK action plan: A) enable burstpool for west-gpu-pool-a (maria to approve), B) lower-priority job eviction policy ON (sanjay to run), C) route 10% of traffic for top enterprise customers to model-small fallback (ana to change routing), D) open urgent change to increase autoscaler max by +30 nodes pending approval.

maria: Approved enabling burstpool. Doing now.

deploy-bot: burstpool toggle command queued by maria: `infra burstpool enable west-gpu-pool-a --reason "inc-6223334444"`

pamela: Sanjay, run eviction on safe pools only, avoid Dedicated tenant nodes unless necessary. Add `--dry-run` first to list candidates.

sanjay: Running eviction dry-run now. sample output:
```
DRY-RUN evict candidates: batch-job-541, nightly-indexer-33, perf-test-12
estimated freed_gpus=6
```

pamela: Good. Proceed with targeted eviction (not full repack).

ana: Routing change pushed: 10% traffic for route /v1/generate for customers CUST-A/CUST-B -> model-small. Monitoring latency.

kevin: Observed immediate queue drop from 4240 -> 3100 after burstpool + evictions + routing change. avg_wait down to 28s. Good signal.

tier2-ops-bot: Note: autoscaler still at max=120. Request to temporarily raise to 150 submitted to infra-admins for emergency change.

maria: CS update posted: "We're mitigating performance issues by routing to smaller model variants and enabling burst capacity. Expect progressive improvement over next 30-60m. We'll follow up with root cause and action items."

customer-success: Customer A acknowledges, asks to be informed before any evictions affecting Dedicated tenants. We avoided that.

pamela: Runtime team, need a post-incident follow-up to address MIG template mismatch and binpacking. Assigning to runtime-oncall.

runtime-oncall: Taking. Initial hypothesis: historical template change migrated some pools to larger MIG slices without updating scheduler binpacker heuristics. We'll run offline binpack simulation and propose migration plan.

ana: Also propose adding a metric for "stranded_gpu_equivalent" so autoscaler can consider fragmentation when deciding to scale.

kevin: Agreed. Also recommend an automated preemptive repack when fragmentation metric crosses threshold to avoid queue growth.

pamela: Current status update: queue 1850, avg_wait=12s, p95_wait=34s. Still monitoring. Leaving incident channel open for handoff to oncall for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated -> monitoring. Handing off to pamela for post-incident review.

pamela: I'm keeping the channel. Will coordinate postmortem and runbook updates (MIG sizing audit, fragmentation metric, emergency autoscaler bump playbook). Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
